Why the US nuclear budget grows while the stockpile of warheads shrinks

Increasing maintenance costs for aging equipment and weapons, security updates against new threats, increased research, more corruption, spreading out the arsenal by making more subs/planes/missiles/silos, increasing safety standards for dealing with radioactive material, inflation causing higher prices, etc.

Basically, we're spending more on fewer nukes the same way we're spending more on fewer soldiers. Nothing new here.
Storage and disposal are huge huge parts of it.

Most of the "modernization" of the nuclear arsenal is directly related to the components and wouldn't really be a modernization of the system from an outside perspective. US ICMBs, for example, still run on VAX minicomputers that are nearly impossible to get parts for at this point, so the plan is to replace them with modern microcomputers... that mimic the old VAXes exactly and slot right into their place.

The B61, for its part, has seen constant development work over the years since it's been deployed, so it's not all a red queen's race.
